title: The double-dual morphism restricts
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a finite commutative ring whose additive exponent is invertible in $k$, and $j:W\to Y$ an etale $k$-morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $T=Y,W$ let $a_T:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure morphism, put $\omega_T=a_T^\times A$ using the ambient compact-support right adjoint [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint], and put $D_TK=R\mathcal Hom_A(K,\omega_T)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $\delta_K:K\to D_TD_TK$ be the transpose of evaluation [lem-weil-duality-pairing], with the usual derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor].

There is a canonical natural isomorphism $\theta:j^*\omega_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_W$. Together with slice restriction of derived internal Hom it induces $\alpha_K:j^*D_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_W(j^*K)$. For every $K\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\alpha_{D_YK}\circ j^*\delta_K=D_W(\alpha_K)\circ\delta_{j^*K}.$$
Thus the isomorphism $(D_W\alpha_K)^{-1}\circ\alpha_{D_YK}:j^*D_YD_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}D_WD_Wj^*K$ carries $j^*\delta_K$ to $\delta_{j^*K}$. In particular $\delta_K$ is an isomorphism if and only if its corresponding double-dual maps on a jointly surjective etale covering by separated finite-type $k$-schemes are isomorphisms.

The restriction calculation also holds on the small pro-etale sites with constant finite coefficients [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]: more generally, for any $\Omega_Y\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ set $\Omega_W=j^*\Omega_Y$, $D_T^\Omega=R\mathcal Hom_A(-,\Omega_T)$ and let $\delta^\Omega$ be the evaluation transpose. Slice restriction gives the same displayed identity with $D^\Omega$ and $\delta^\Omega$ [lem-weil-duality-pairing, def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. Consequently it applies to a finite pro-etale realization with its specified compatible dualizing objects. This clause concerns ordinary constant-ring module categories; it does not assert an unconditional ambient pro-etale exceptional adjoint or identify them with condensed coefficient categories.

proof.text: The affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian: the only ideals of a field are zero and the unit ideal. Its underlying space is a singleton, so it and every intersection of its affine opens are quasi-compact; the base of Nagata is therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $Y$ and $W$ are Noetherian. Nagata [thm-nagata-compactification] compactifies $a_Y$ and $a_W$; their proper compactification spaces are finite type over $k$ and hence Noetherian by the same finite-type lemma. Thus their ambient right adjoints exist by [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. The morphism $j$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-cancellation], since $a_W=a_Yj$ is separated. It is locally finite type because etale includes unramifiedness [def-weil-unramified-morphism], whose definition includes local finite type; it is quasi-compact because inverse images of affine opens of $Y$ are open subschemes of the Noetherian scheme $W$, hence quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The compact-support assertion of [lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], applied to $f=a_Y$, $u=j$, and the constant input $A$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k$, now gives the natural isomorphism $\theta:j^*\omega_Y\cong\omega_W$. This use is only on ordinary etale categories and only over the finite ring $A$.

proof.text: For etale restriction use the proved source-library strong monoidal left derived inverse image and its braided compatibility (leftDerivedUpperStar_μ_map_braiding_hom). The source theorem isIso_ihomComparison_leftDerivedUpperStar_of_etale proves its closed comparison invertible. Transport along leftDerivedUpperStarIsoMapDerivedCategory to the exact derived restriction. The prescribed braiding is constructed directly as the descended Koszul braiding.

For a braided strong monoidal closed functor G, postcompose its internal-Hom comparison with theta. Naturality gives alpha. The defining equation for ihomComparison proves evaluation compatibility. Apply the proved categorical identity MonoidalClosed.map_toIhomIhom_comp_dualComparison; cancel the inverse comparison to obtain the transported double-dual identity. The private canonicalRestriction and canonicalRestrictionTransport implement this argument without any new hole.

Apply the source-library derived etale-cover isomorphism detector to delta. To accommodate an arbitrary universe of cover indices, choose one member and one point above each y in Y; this gives a point-indexed cover. Transport its left-derived comparison along the exact-derived natural isomorphism. Locally the delta is conjugate by the proved restriction comparison, so isIso_comp_right_iff gives the desired equivalence. Empty Y is included.

For pro-etale restriction derive the tensor comparison using the proved generic Functor.leftDerivedTensorComparison and its homotopy localization square. Conjugate by leftDerivedFunctorIsoMapDerivedCategory; the factorization identity gives exactly IsNormalizedDeltaRestrictionTensor. This proves the tensor-normalization existence theorem without a new assumption.

Apply [lem-weil-proetale-derived-restriction-closed-monoidal] to the normalized tensor comparison. This supplies the compatible strong monoidal structure, Koszul braided identity and invertible native closed comparison. Apply the same categorical argument of step 3 with arbitrary Omega and the identity on its restriction. Thus no pro-etale exceptional adjoint is asserted.
